pharm: Non-acidic NSAID prodrug converted in the liver to the active metabolite 6-methoxy-2-naphthylacetic acid (6-MNA), which inhibits cyclooxygenase and prostaglandin synthesis.
quick: 1000 mg once daily; may increase to 1500-2000 mg/day (max 2000 mg/day)
Take with or without food; food increases absorption
Avoid from 30 weeks (premature ductus closure); caution from 20 weeks
Reduce dose in CrCl <50; CrCl 30-49 max 1500 mg/day; <30 max 1000 mg/day
Caution; monitor LFTs, discontinue if liver disease develops
Blood pressure, renal function, CBC, LFTs, GI bleeding signs
summary: Nabumetone is a once-daily nonselective NSAID prodrug used to relieve the signs and symptoms of osteoarthritis and rheumatoid arthritis. It is converted in the liver to the active metabolite 6-MNA. Like all NSAIDs it carries boxed warnings for cardiovascular thrombotic events and serious gastrointestinal bleeding/ulceration, is contraindicated in the perioperative CABG setting, and should be avoided in late pregnancy. Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration.
indications: Relief of signs and symptoms of osteoarthritis
Relief of signs and symptoms of rheumatoid arthritis

dosage.t: As a single dose or in two divided doses
dosage.n: Max 2000 mg/day; doses above 2000 mg not studied

admin: May be taken with or without food; food increases the rate of absorption and raises peak 6-MNA by about one-third
Use the lowest effective dose for the shortest duration consistent with treatment goals
Avoid concomitant use of other NSAIDs or aspirin for analgesia
moa: Nabumetone is an inactive prodrug; after hepatic conversion its active metabolite 6-methoxy-2-naphthylacetic acid (6-MNA) inhibits cyclooxygenase (COX-1 and COX-2), reducing prostaglandin synthesis and producing anti-inflammatory, analgesic, and antipyretic effects.

absolute: History of asthma, urticaria, or allergic-type reaction to aspirin or other NSAIDs (aspirin triad)
Perioperative use in the setting of coronary artery bypass graft (CABG) surgery
relative: Active GI bleeding or peptic ulcer disease
Severe heart failure or uncontrolled hypertension

preg: Avoid from 30 weeks of gestation onward due to risk of premature closure of the fetal ductus arteriosus; use at 20 weeks or later may cause fetal renal dysfunction and oligohydramnios. Before 30 weeks, use only if clearly needed.
lact: It is not known whether nabumetone/6-MNA is excreted in human milk (present in rat milk); weigh the benefit of breastfeeding against potential risk.
renal: No adjustment if CrCl 50 mL/min or above. For CrCl 30-49 mL/min, start at 750 mg/day (max 1500 mg/day); for CrCl below 30 mL/min, start at 500 mg/day (max 1000 mg/day). Avoid in advanced renal disease.
hepatic: Conversion to and clearance of 6-MNA may be reduced in severe hepatic impairment; monitor liver function and discontinue if clinical signs of liver disease develop.

major: Aspirin / other NSAIDs - additive GI toxicity
moderate: ACE inhibitors, ARBs, beta-blockers - reduced antihypertensive effect and renal risk
interactions.food: Food increases absorption and peak 6-MNA levels
interactions.alcohol: Increases the risk of gastrointestinal bleeding
interactions.diagnostics: May affect renal function tests and prolong bleeding time.

serious: GI bleeding, ulceration, or perforation (may be silent and fatal)

monitoring: Signs and symptoms of GI bleeding
Edema and body weight in patients with heart failure
counsel: Report stomach pain, black or bloody stools, or vomiting blood - GI bleeding can occur without warning
Seek urgent care for chest pain, weakness, slurred speech, or shortness of breath
Do not use around the time of heart bypass surgery or with other NSAIDs/aspirin for pain
Avoid NSAIDs after about 30 weeks of pregnancy
Limit alcohol; take the lowest effective dose for the shortest time
pk: Symptomatic relief over days; analgesic effect within hours
Active metabolite 6-MNA peaks ~3 hours after a dose
pearls: A prodrug - it is inactive until the liver converts it to 6-MNA
Boxed warnings for cardiovascular thrombotic events and serious GI bleeding apply as with all NSAIDs
Long half-life of the active metabolite allows convenient once-daily dosing and aids adherence
Relatively favorable upper-GI tolerability, but serious GI risk still exists
Highly protein-bound (>99%) so hemodialysis is not useful in overdose
missed: Take the missed dose as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for the next dose, skip the missed dose - do not take a double dose.
overdose: Symptoms include lethargy, drowsiness, nausea, vomiting, and epigastric pain. Manage supportively; activated charcoal may be given if presentation is early. Because nabumetone is highly protein bound, dialysis is not useful. Monitor for GI bleeding, renal function, and acid-base status.
